story.title: Zelensky Opposes Wartime Elections, Citing Risks for Ukraine
story.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has rejected calls for wartime elections, stating that such a move would be highly dangerous and could split the country. His comments follow a proposal from former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who was recently dismissed. A recent poll indicated that only 15% of Ukrainians support holding elections during the ongoing conflict.

timeline_highlights.title: Ousted Ukrainian Defense Minister Calls for Wartime Elections Amid Ongoing Conflict
timeline_highlights.summary: Mykhailo Fedorov, Ukraine's recently dismissed Defense Minister, has called for presidential elections to be held despite the ongoing war with Russia. In a significant challenge to President Volodymyr Zelensky, Fedorov argued that the country is experiencing a crisis of governance. His remarks come as Ukraine remains under martial law, which prohibits elections during wartime.
key_facts: Mykhailo Fedorov was dismissed as Defense Minister last month.
Fedorov's call for elections is the first of its kind since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022.
Ukrainian law currently prohibits elections under martial law.

event_overview.title: About Ukraine Politics
event_overview.subject: Ukraine Politics
event_overview.summary: This event concerns Ukraine’s debate over whether to hold presidential, parliamentary or local elections while the country remains under martial law during Russia’s full-scale invasion. The issue combines legal restrictions on voting with practical questions about security, occupied territory, military service and the ability of displaced citizens to participate.

facts.label: Martial-law start
facts.value: Ukraine imposed martial law nationwide beginning at 5:30 a.m. on February 24, 2022, citing Russia’s military aggression; the Verkhovna Rada approved the presidential decree.

facts.label: Legal restriction on elections
facts.value: Ukraine’s Law on the Legal Regime of Martial Law bars presidential, parliamentary and local elections, as well as national and local referendums, during martial law.

facts.label: Constitutional continuity
facts.value: If the Verkhovna Rada’s term expires during martial law, its authority continues until the first sitting of a newly elected parliament after martial law is lifted; the legal framework also provides continuity for the presidency until a successor takes office.

facts.label: Election administration
facts.value: Ukraine’s Central Election Commission suspended electoral processes after martial law was introduced on February 24, 2022; post-martial-law election planning must address the resumption and scheduling of elections.

facts.label: Core practical constraints
facts.value: Official post-war election analysis identifies security conditions, occupied or recently liberated areas, population displacement, voter registration and election-administration capacity as major issues for any eventual nationwide vote.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the August 19–24, 2026 political debate over wartime elections and related scrutiny of Ukraine’s leadership, not the full history of Ukraine’s electoral system, martial law, corruption cases or the war.

explore_lenses.label: What would have to change before a vote?
explore_lenses.title: Martial law is the immediate legal barrier
explore_lenses.summary: Ukraine’s current martial-law framework prohibits presidential, parliamentary and local elections. Ending or changing that framework would be a prerequisite, but practical rules for a post-war vote remain unsettled.

claims.text: Ukraine’s Law on the Legal Regime of Martial Law prohibits presidential, parliamentary and local elections while martial law is in force.
The Central Election Commission said it stopped electoral processes after martial law was imposed in February 2022, citing the martial-law law’s election restriction.

Ukraine’s Electoral Code says a decision to call elections whose process was suspended or had not begun because of martial law should be made within one month of martial law ending; election specialists have argued that a longer transition may be needed.

The Constitution provides that the president exercises powers until a newly elected president takes office, a provision cited by election-law analysts in explaining continuity while elections are postponed.

points: Ukraine’s Law on the Legal Regime of Martial Law prohibits presidential, parliamentary and local elections while martial law is in force.
The Central Election Commission said it stopped electoral processes after martial law was imposed in February 2022, citing the martial-law law’s election restriction.

Ukraine’s Electoral Code says a decision to call elections whose process was suspended or had not begun because of martial law should be made within one month of martial law ending; election specialists have argued that a longer transition may be needed.

The Constitution provides that the president exercises powers until a newly elected president takes office, a provision cited by election-law analysts in explaining continuity while elections are postponed.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: No announced legal timetable or agreed election framework was identified for holding a nationwide vote during the current war.

explore_lenses.label: Why do Zelensky and Fedorov disagree?
explore_lenses.title: Democratic renewal versus feasibility and security
explore_lenses.summary: Fedorov argues Ukraine should develop a lawful way to restore electoral competition during a prolonged war. Zelensky says no credible plan has yet shown how a vote could be safe, inclusive and legitimate under wartime conditions.

claims.text: Fedorov called for a “legal, safe, and realistic mechanism” for wartime elections and said voting rights would need to be protected for service members, Ukrainians abroad and people in frontline areas.
Fedorov’s stated argument is that Russia should not determine when Ukrainians are able to choose their government.
Zelensky said an election now would pose an enormous risk and could split the country; he said Ukraine’s partners had not produced a plan to conduct one safely, legitimately and democratically.

In 2023, Zelensky identified voting access for military personnel and displaced Ukrainians abroad, funding, security at frontline polling places and international observation as conditions for a democratic wartime election.

In 2023, Zelensky identified voting access for military personnel and displaced Ukrainians abroad, funding, security at frontline polling places and international observation as conditions for a democratic wartime election.

story_report.summary: President Volodymyr Zelensky rejected former defense minister Mykhailo Fedorov’s call for wartime elections, arguing that a vote would pose an enormous risk and could divide Ukraine. The proposal has no announced route to a nationwide ballot: martial-law rules prohibit presidential, parliamentary and local elections while they remain in force, and the Central Election Commission halted electoral processes after martial law was imposed in February 2022. A poll cited in reports found 15% support for holding elections now.

sections.heading: Martial Law Governs Election Timing
sections.body: Ukraine’s Law on the Legal Regime of Martial Law bars presidential, parliamentary and local elections during martial law. The Electoral Code says decisions to call elections suspended or not begun because of martial law should be made within one month after martial law ends, though election specialists have argued that a longer transition could be necessary. The Constitution also provides for the president to exercise powers until a newly elected president takes office.

sections.heading: Fedorov and Zelensky Differ on Safeguards
sections.body: Fedorov has called for a legal, safe and realistic wartime-election mechanism, saying voting rights must be protected for service members, Ukrainians abroad and people in frontline areas. His stated position is that Russia should not determine when Ukrainians can choose their government. Zelensky has said Ukraine’s partners have not offered a plan for an election that is safe, legitimate and democratic; in 2023, he identified military and overseas voting access, funding, frontline security and international observation as necessary conditions.

unresolved.text: No announced legal timetable or agreed election framework has been identified for a nationwide wartime vote, and neither side has publicly presented a detailed, legally adopted mechanism addressing access, security and observation concerns.

related_stories.title: Kushner and Jeffries Meet Ahead of Midterm Elections
related_stories.summary: Jared Kushner met with Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries in New York City to discuss potential cooperation between Democrats and Trump as the midterm elections approach. The meeting comes as control of the House is at stake in the upcoming November elections, with Democrats expected to gain an advantage. Topics discussed included housing, immigration, and the rising cost of living.

related_stories.title: U.S. Marines Cancel Joint Drills with South Korea Due to Iran War Constraints
related_stories.summary: The U.S. Marines have canceled a planned joint military drill with South Korea, citing force constraints related to the ongoing Iran war. This decision was communicated in June, following President Trump's recent order to reduce the duration of another military exercise, the Ulchi Freedom Shield, from 11 days to five. The cancellation reflects adjustments in U.S. military commitments amid international conflicts.

related_stories.title: Landfill Collapse in Conakry Results in At Least 30 Fatalities
related_stories.summary: A landfill collapse in Conakry, Guinea, has resulted in at least 30 deaths and six injuries. The incident occurred after heavy rains, leading to the destruction of homes in the area. Emergency teams have initiated a search and rescue operation to find survivors among the debris.
